title.narrative: Strengthening Access to Integrated Healthcare Services for Vulnerable Populations in Damboa LGA, Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project seeks to address the critical health needs of vulnerable populations in Damboa Local Government Area (LGA) of Borno State, Nigeria. The overarching goal is to improve access to quality, life-saving services and strengthen community resilience through an impact assessment multi-pronged approach that integrates preventive and curative healthcare services.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project aims to strengthen access to life-saving integrated primary health services for internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, people in extremely hard-to-reach areas, and host communities, ensuring equitable, safe, and accountable service delivery. Through integrated health interventions, this project will enhance the well-being and resilience of affected individuals, particularly women, girls, and persons with disabilities (PWDs). The project prioritizes a humanitarian-development nexus approach by reinforcing existing health infrastructure and expanding outreach through mobile medical teams, thereby improving the quality and continuum of care.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe health intervention will focus on ensuring access to essential services including immunization, antenatal care, treatment of common illnesses, and mental health and psychosocial support strengthening early detection and rapid response to outbreaks, especially cholera, measles, and malaria provision of immediate treatment for SAM and sexual reproductive health.. These will be achieved through a multifaceted approach: Firstly, the project will directly support three (3) existing health facilities in the LGA, ensuring they are adequately equipped with essential medical drugs, supplies, and trained personnel to deliver quality inpatient and outpatient care, including GBV Prevention and Response Services. Secondly, mobile medical teams comprised of nurses, community health extension workers (CHEWs), and community health volunteers (CHVs) will be deployed to remote areas, IDP camps, and other hard-to-reach locations. Thirdly, there will be engagement of the RCCE team, which consists of CHEWs and CHVs, for the purpose of regular and timely health education. These teams will provide primary healthcare services, treatment for minor ailments, reproductive and maternal health services, counseling and psychosocial support, health education, and actively conduct case searches for Acute Watery Diarrhea (AWD) and Cholera. The RCCE team will lead efforts in risk communication, disease outbreak prevention, sexual and reproductive health (SRH), PSEA, hygiene and sanitation promotion, and response measures.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtRecognizing the pervasive nature of GBV in conflict-affected settings, the project will integrate GBV prevention and response strategies across all activities. Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials will be strategically employed to raise awareness of GBV, including prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), within the target communities.lt/pgt
